title: WW2 British postal-censorship manual steganograms, TNA KV 2/2424 (Schmeh Top 50 no. 33)

documents.shelfmark: TNA KV 2/2424, manual p. 17, Illustration No. 14

plaintext.source: The manual gives the message in English translation only: 'Oil has arrived, everything is ready. Gustav available for the appointed day.'

transcription.source: Schmeh's 2017 photograph and the TNA digital copy; a 2016 blog reader's fragment AATHUT
transcription.notes: Pen marks of 0.1-0.3 mm are 2-5 px in the best image; no transcription made. Year is the date of the covering note (25 Nov 1943), not of the example.

documents.shelfmark: TNA KV 2/2424, manual p. 14, Illustration No. 13

plaintext.source: Manual: 'Heavy reinforcements for the enemy expected hourly' (figures 1-3); 'Before Arras' (signature, French shorthand).

transcription.notes: Carriers (hem and cape trims, signature strokes) not resolvable; no transcription made. Language of the Morse message not established.

system.summary: Steganographic Morse in pen marks beside map tram lines, the German plaintext Caesar-shifted by -11; the drawing hides Morse in dress trims and Duployé shorthand in the signature.
system.notes: The shift is given by the manual (11 positions); the 2016 fragment AATHUT +11 = LLESFE (ALLES FERTIG) fixes its direction. Caesar shift, so key_order is not applicable.

prior_solution.where: The manual states both plaintexts but not the mechanics; blog readers read AATHUT (2016) and Arras in the signature (2020)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: AATHUT +11 = LLESFE from ALLES FERTIG: map carries German shifted -11 in Morse; predicted mark sequences for candidate wordings.
Unrolled four tram bands and measured run lengths: ordinary tram-line fill, not Morse.
'French shorthand' points to Duployé, supporting the 2020 Arras reading over the Stolze-Schrey one.
Mark detector along the Raadhuisstraat band: 24 candidates whose widths do not separate into dots and dashes.
Downloaded TNA's digital KV 2/2424: pixel-identical to the blog scan, no resolution gain.

outcome.method_basis: The known plaintexts stated in the manual and the 2016 'AATHUT' fragment fixed the map's shift direction (-11), but the Morse pen marks and the shorthand signature are below the resolution of every available scan (TNA KV 2/2424), so no text was read.
outcome.notes: Blocked on image resolution; needs a 1,200 dpi scan of pp. 14 and 17 from Kew.
